description: GraphQL API that exposes Fabric data (lakehouses, warehouses, SQL databases) as a typed GraphQL schema. Enables applications to query Fabric data via standard GraphQL queries and mutations.

definition_parts.description: Datasource binding: {datasources:[{sourceItemId, sourceWorkspaceId, sourceType, objects:[{graphqlType, sourceObject:'schema.table', sourceObjectType:'Table'|'View'}]}]}. The bound object MUST have a primary key (server errors KeyFieldsEmpty otherwise).
GraphQL SDL — auto-GENERATED by the server once graphql-definition.json is applied (you do not author it to wire a source).

notes: updateDefinition is LRO. fabio graphql-api update-definition --file accepts EITHER a raw GraphQL SDL (wrapped as schema.graphql) OR a full definition envelope ({definition:{parts:[...]}} or {parts:[...]}) passed through verbatim — use the envelope with a graphql-definition.json part to WIRE the API to a SQL source.
To wire a source you push graphql-definition.json (NOT schema.graphql); the server rejects a lone schema.graphql with ALM.MissingDefinitionParts and generates schema.graphql itself.

sourceType: use 'SqlAnalyticsEndpoint' (verified) — it covers a lakehouse SQL endpoint, a warehouse, AND a Fabric SQL database (point sourceItemId at the DB's auto-created SQL analytics endpoint item, NOT the SQLDatabase item; 'SqlDatabase' is rejected as an invalid sourceType).
sourceItemId is the SQL analytics endpoint ID (not the lakehouse/warehouse/SQL-database item ID)
Each objects[] entry needs graphqlType + sourceObject ('schema.table') + sourceObjectType; the bound table must have a primary key.
Query endpoint: POST /graphqlApis/{id}/graphql with {"query":"..."}. The generated query field is the pluralized/camelCased type (e.g. Widget -> widgets { items { ... } }).
Introspection (__schema) blocked by default unless tenant setting enabled
